We just don't spend money like that - especially when we really aren't football fans in the first place and we aren't wealthy. The day is ending up costing us over $500 now, which is a lot of money for us to miss... And it's making us feel different about our neighbors now.

text:
AITA for not wanting to keep my bedroom door closed because my roommate's cat prefers spending time with me?
I live with two roommates, one of whom has a cat. There’s been an odd situation developing regarding the cat and my bedroom.
I pretty much always leave my bedroom door open when I’m home. I’m used to it, and I like being able to see and hear what’s going on around the house. The cat is allowed to wander around, so naturally they frequently come into my room.
The cat and I are particularly close. I’m clearly their favorite person in the house. Whenever I’m home, they follow me around, sit at my feet, and generally want to be wherever I am. My room has also basically become their safe space, and they spend a lot of time in there hanging out near me.
Recently, my roommate told me he doesn't want the cat going into my room anymore and wants me to keep my bedroom door closed from now on.
I’m trying to respect that. The cat is his, so I understand that he gets to decide where the cat is and isn't allowed to go. I haven't been deliberately encouraging the cat to come into my room.
The problem is that I really don't like having my door closed all the time. It makes me feel isolated from the rest of the house, and it's just not how I'm accustomed to living. Having my door open has never been an issue before, and now I feel like I have to keep my room shut off simply because the cat might want to come inside.
My roommate's reasoning is that he misses when the cat would spend more time in the living room, be more social with everyone, and greet people when they came home. Since becoming attached to me, the cat now spends much of their time in my room toward the back of the house.
Given the circumstances, I’m pretty convinced my roommate is at least partly jealous of the relationship I've developed with his cat. I understand why he might feel that way, but I don't think either of us can control who the cat chooses to spend time with.
What's also strange is that even when I keep my door closed, the cat still spends a lot of time sitting outside my door. So I'm not sure closing the door actually solves the underlying problem—it just prevents the cat from being inside while leaving them right outside.
I’m willing to respect the rule that the cat isn't allowed in my room. What I'm questioning is whether that means I should have to keep my bedroom door closed 24/7 to enforce it.
It seems like there might be other ways to encourage the cat to spend more time in the living room—playing with them there, giving treats there, moving some of their favorite things there, etc.
AITA for not wanting to keep my bedroom door closed all the time, even though I'm trying to respect my roommate's wishes about his cat? And are there any other solutions I'm overlooking that could accomplish what my roommate wants without requiring me to keep my door closed constantly?
label: nta

text:
AITA for asking two older men to leave our table at a busy pub?
I (23F) went out for a drink and meal with my friend (23F) the other day. We both work full-time and Monday is basically the only day we can meet, so we hadn't seen each other in 2–3 weeks and were really excited to catch up.

We went to a fairly popular chain pub in the UK. It was quite busy, although there were still some tables available when we arrived. We ordered our food and drinks and sat at a booth-style table. The table was definitely big enough for four people, but there were only two of us. We chose it because the pub was busy, and we thought that if a larger group needed the table, we'd obviously move or offer them the space.

We were sitting there chatting when two older men, probably in their 70s or 80s, came over and sat down at our table without asking.

One of them put his coat around the chair opposite me, while the other actually slid into the booth next to me.

My friend and I basically just stopped talking and looked at each other awkwardly because we weren't expecting anyone to sit with us. One of the men just said, "Boy, it's so busy today."

We pointed out that there seemed to be other tables available and that a table behind us had actually just become free. We were trying to hint that we'd rather they sat somewhere else rather than directly joining us.

The man sitting next to me basically said that they were just going to sit here.

We then mentioned that we'd already ordered food and drinks, maybe they thought we'd be leaving soon? He said that they were getting food too and smiled.

At that point, his friend picked up his coat and said something along the lines of, "Come on, it's clear they don't want us here."

The man sitting in the booth next to me then stood up and said, "It's clear when we're not wanted."

They left and we carried on with our meal. But felt a tad bit awkward and off after that as to us it just felt really odd

Now I'm wondering whether we were actually being rude? I understand that the table technically seats four people, and I don't have a problem sharing a table if a pub is genuinely full. But in this case, there appeared to be other tables available.

It also felt particularly strange to me that they chose to sit directly at a table with two young women who were already eating/drinking, rather than simply asking if they could share?

So, AITA for making it clear that we didn't want them to sit with us? Is sharing tables with strangers something that's considered completely normal in UK pubs. Should we have just left it and pretended like they weren't there

EDIT: just a quick edit to explain some things, if the men were young we would've still been creeped out. I can see what people mean by their ages not being necessary in this, I only mentioned it to give as much context as possible.

I love talking to new people on nights out, there's honestly nothing better and when it's the right mood I can sit and talk to a stranger for ages. But I have been going through a lot of personal stuff this month, nearly lost someone close to me so I personally just wanted to have a nice drink and meal with my close friend and talk about it because it's been a really tough month.

the booth I was sat in was a weird right angle booth so I was trapped in which is why I felt particularly uncomfortable

And yes it was a Spoons (Wetherspoons) I assumed it was mostly Americans on here so thought if I just said spoons they'd be confused 😂

I also should mentioned about 5 minutes after they had left, I got up to go get some condiments for me and my friend. And saw a different area that was blocked off from our point of view in the booth. And pretty much the ENTIRE area was free

text:
AITA for not telling my cousin about something I overheard?
A few weeks ago, I was on my computer while my mom was on the phone. I wasn't intentionally listening, but I could hear parts of the conversation in the background. I thought she was probably talking to a family member, but I didn't actually know who she was talking to.
From what I overheard, I gathered that the person my mom was talking to wanted some space from their spouse and might be staying somewhere else for a while. That was basically all I knew. I didn't know who the person was, what the situation actually was, or whether I had even understood the conversation correctly.
Later, my cousin told me that this was about her parents. I immediately responded, “I know.”
She was confused, so I immediately explained that I didn't actually know. I had only overheard part of a conversation, didn't know who my mom was talking to, and had no idea that the conversation was about her parents.
At the time, she seemed to take it relatively lightly and even joked that I must have it out for her that day. We moved on from the conversation.
Apparently, she thought about it more afterward and became upset. Instead of contacting me directly, she asked someone to ask my mom to ask me to apologize.
Eventually, she did contact me and explained that what upset her wasn't just that I said “I know.” She was also upset that I had apparently heard the conversation before she told me and didn't immediately tell her what I had overheard.
This is where I feel like we fundamentally disagree.
Even if I had been 100% certain that the conversation I overheard was about her parents, I still would not have gone to my cousin and told her about it before her mom had a chance to tell her herself. It isn’t my information to share.
I absolutely acknowledge that saying “I know” was a bad choice of words. I understand why that made it sound like I had known about her parents the whole time and deliberately kept it from her. I should have phrased it differently.
But I don't feel that I should apologize for not telling her immediately about the conversation. She seems to feel that I should have told her even if I wasn't sure who it was about.
Another part of this is that she didn't actually talk to me about how upset she was for quite a while. She was apparently thinking about it and getting more upset, but I didn't know that. She gave me the silent treatment for an half an hour without telling me what was wrong, I just figured she was overstimulated or something. She felt like I was being defensive and making excuses, while I felt like I was explaining because the actual circumstances mattered.
So I can accept responsibility for saying “I know” when I should have chosen my words better. But I don't think I should apologize for not immediately telling her something that I wasn't sure about, and I especially don't think I should have told her even if I had been certain, because I believe that decision belonged to her mom.
So, AITA?
label: nta

AITA for defending my husband after my mom called him cheap and disrespectful over $14 change?

After we got the food, it started pouring. While we were waiting for the rain to stop, my husband asked my mom if she had gotten the change.
My mom later told me when we were alone that she was holding onto the change because she wanted to buy something else. And she was offended by his question. She called my husband disrespectful. She said she had planned to return the money, but the way he asked made her feel like he thought she was going to pocket it.

I told her I didn’t want to keep hearing her ranting over $14 and that she should take it up with my husband as I didn’t want to hear it anymore. She ended up texting him a week later, telling him how disappointed she was.

My husband was mortified and genuinely didn’t understand what he had done wrong. He apologized to keep the peace, but she never acknowledged his apology.

I refused to side with my mom because I think turning a $14 misunderstanding into a family conflict is ridiculous. We kept arguing, and I may have said some hurtful things about her husband. I asked her why she couldn’t just let it go when my husband clearly didn’t intend to be disrespectful. I brought up how she asked me to pay half of a $1,000 birthday gift for my stepdad and I gladly obliged even though he’s not my father. I don’t even spend that much on my own father, and my stepdad married my mom when I was 18. I still call him my stepdad, but he is really just my mom’s husband.

My mom then called me ungrateful and threatened to cut ties with me. She said her husband had loaned me money to buy car to pay for college before, and had helped me more than my own father (my dad didn’t have a lot and lived in a poor country). She also brought up all the things she’s done for us, including cooking and buying us things, as if we were ungrateful. She is generous, but I sometimes feel like she uses her generosity against us during arguments.

This isn’t the first time she has threatened to cut me off during an argument, but it’s the first time my husband has been involved.

She moved in at the end of May. The first payment came in on June 5th, no problem. Then she lost her job.

In mid-August I used a service industry contact to get her a good opportunity, a fast track to management. She was visibly disappointed because it was another service job. She interviewed anyway and got it start date September 1st. She had a birthday trip home planned first and was to start after that.

AITA for not helping my elderly, disabled neighbor?
I 27F live in an apartment with my boyfriend 28M. I have a neighbor who lives across the hall from me who is older (maybe 60s) and disabled. I’m not sure what his disability is, but he uses a walker and has a sling on one arm. He needs his other arm to support his weight on the walker, so he can’t really pick up anything heavy.

A few weeks ago he was leaving his door open and would try to catch me any time I entered or left my apartment. He asked me to purchase cat food, cigarettes, and Pedialyte and gave me money to do so. I dropped off the things he needed and he was very grateful.

I didn’t see him for about two weeks. The other day his door was open and he caught me while I was leaving. He told me he had been taken to rehab and both of his cats starved to death in his apartment while he was gone because he didn’t have anyone to take care of them.

I have a cat of my own and this absolutely mortified me. I have thought about these poor cats that were right across the hall from me nonstop for the past 3 days. I have cried over cats that I only met once. My boyfriend keeps reiterating that I am not at fault and couldn’t possibly have known what was happening behind a closed door. I know this, but it’s been sitting on me so heavily.

He has since asked me if I’m able to dedicate some time to help him. He said he needs help taking out his garbage, doing his laundry, general housekeeping, shopping, and cleaning the litter boxes, which are still filthy. I told him I work full time and am also a full-time student and wouldn’t be able to make that kind of commitment. He said it would only be an hour or two a day.

He has a shopping cart, so I told him to put his trash in it and wheel it into the hallway and I’d take it out when I see it. But he also told me he doesn’t have clean clothes and asked me to put his laundry in the washer and dryer. He said he would give me money for the machines, but I do not feel comfortable doing this man’s laundry.

I don’t know this man or anything about him. I don’t even know his name. I’m worried that because I made myself available for a few things, the list will keep piling on and I’ll end up as his primary caretaker. I also don’t know why he doesn’t have a nurse or someone coming to assist him, especially after just getting out of rehab.

I talked to my friend, who’s a nurse, and she said an aide should have been assigned to him for home health care unless he turned one down. She also said I was selfish for not being willing to help someone in need.

I feel bad because he’s lonely, he lost his cats, and he needs help. But I don’t know this man, and I feel like an hour or two a day is a lot to ask of someone you only know because you live across the hall from each other.

AITA for not being willing to help more?

Edit: he has never stopped my boyfriend or asked him for help when he sees him come and go. He mostly lays on his couch in front of the door and is completely nude except for a sheet that he uses to cover himself because he doesn’t have clean clothes.

text:
AITA for for changing departments only two months after being promoted?
I work in auditing in the public sector and have been in the same department for a few years. This is my first permanent full-time job since university, and the work is quite independent, so most of my day-to-day interaction is with my manager.

I’ve worked hard and received very positive feedback from all three managers I’ve had. About six months after I first started, my manager at the time encouraged me to apply for a vacant senior position. I didn’t apply because I was still new and didn’t feel ready. I assumed another opportunity would come up once I had more experience, but it took several years.

A senior position finally became available recently. My current manager, a previous manager and several colleagues encouraged me to apply, and I was successful. I’ve only been in the position for about two months.

Now a role has opened in another department within the same organisation. It’s an area I’ve been interested in for a while, and the position is at the same level and salary as my current role. I’ve heard that the department has recently become busier and is looking for more staff, so this may be a rare opportunity to move into that area.

I haven’t applied yet because I feel guilty. My manager and colleagues supported me, recognised my work and encouraged me to apply for the promotion. I genuinely appreciate that. Applying elsewhere so soon makes me feel as though I would be letting them down or taking their support for granted.

However, I’m also questioning whether my current work is sustainable for me. I like the work and have learned a lot, but it’s extremely complex and demanding. The deadlines often feel almost impossible, and getting to this point required me to spend many evenings and weekends working.

I’m proud of what I’ve achieved, but I don’t want that level of sacrifice to become normal. Promotion opportunities in my department are also quite rare. My impression is that progressing further would require me to keep demonstrating an exceptional level of commitment and results, and I’m not sure I can maintain that pace.

I was also recently diagnosed with an autoimmune condition. It isn’t severe, but I need to manage it properly and make some lifestyle changes. I’d also like to keep open the possibility of having children in the near future. I’m not looking for an easy job with no responsibility, but I do want enough time and energy outside work to look after my health and enjoy my life.

A close friend thinks I should stay longer because I’ve built a strong reputation in my current department. They believe I may have a better chance of eventually progressing into an even more senior role there, whereas moving would mean starting again and rebuilding my reputation.

WIBTA if I applied for the other position only two months after my manager and colleagues supported me in getting promoted? Do I owe it to them to stay for a reasonable period, or is it fair to prioritise my health and long-term work-life balance?

AITA for anonymously reporting my coach to the board?

For the youth team, he is in charge of planning & running practices. My role is to help execute them, manage the girls & basically be a “mom”.

I'll be honest I don't like him. I feel he talks down to me & others, but that is NOT why I reported him.

My issue is the quality of his practices. They're far below what the girls are capable of & they spend a lot of time sitting around instead of being active.

There's also a language barrier. He doesn't speak the girls' language. Neither do I fluently, but I've lived here for 1.5 years and understand it & speak enough for the girls to understand me.

I was approached with concerns by parents & encouraged to contact the youth board.

I didn't confront him first because I've challenged him before. Where he refused to speak to me for the rest of practice. He has also spontaneously told me to run practices without warning. When I've said I haven't prepared anything because planning is his responsibility, his response was: “I'm the boss, so I decide. Therefore, you've prepared something.”

Considering he also has authority over me as a player, I wasn't comfortable formally confronting him.

I contacted the board anonymously. They know it's me, but I've asked them not to reveal my identity when they address the issue.

Importantly, I didn't list everything I thought he did wrong. I know I personally dislike him and didn't want to bias them. I even had my mom help make my message neutral.

This is the entire message I sent (translated):

Hi Sue.

I've been encouraged by parents of the girls to contact the board regarding the youth teams.

I could easily tell you one thing or another, but I think the best solution would be for one or two board members to observe some of the girls' practices.

That way, you can form your own impression.

Afterwards, I'd like a meeting where we can discuss whether we have the same view of the practices.

Kind regards

The board came without telling him why. Afterwards, they told me they also thought the situation with his coaching was bad.

Ironically, during that practice he put me in charge of the youngest girls. I hadn't been told to plan anything, as that's normally his duty, so I had to improvise.

This meant I was unknowingly being evaluated on the same basis as him while running a practice I'd had zero opportunity to prepare. which I'm okay with, because I wanted the board to see a completely normal practice, not a prepared “show practice.”

I did go behind his back. He wasn't told about the complaint or observation, & I didn't give him a chance to improve before involving the board.

AITA for anonymously reporting him & asking the board to observe his coaching rather than confronting him directly?

AITA for not having my brother say goodbye to our mum

My stepfather is on a business trip so can't drive my siblings to school. My sister (10f) is on a week long school trip. So it's come to me (20f) to take responsibility of the house, since I'm unemployed, having just finished my studies. (Hopefully hearing about a job offer this week!)
This isn't new — even during my studies I held a lot of responsibility at home: chores, cooking, cleaning, childcare. My mother calls me her household manager. With my step father gone, my mother can't drive and has to work first thing (when he's here, she only leaves around 10am, but now leaves early).

I arranged a paid driver to take my brother to school at 8am. I wake at 7:30 to prep his snack box and get ready, while my mother dresses him.
Today I looked around the apartment and couldn't find or hear her, so assumed she'd gone downstairs to her office (the complex has office spaces). I didn't call out for her — if she's in her bathroom she leaves the door open, closing it only after she's done. So I assumed she'd left and said her goodbyes already. It was 7:57, my brother needed his shoes on, but he's little and slow, so I rushed him and we left.

The second we reached the driver, my mother phoned screaming, demanding why I didn't call for her first. I explained, but she said that didn't matter.
We drove to school, I came home and showered. While showering, my mother barged into the bathroom (I have no privacy at home) screaming that I hadn't let my brother say goodbye to her — she could've been in a car accident and never said her last words to him. I don't get why, since she doesn't drive and works from home. She called me the most selfish person at home, said I only care about my boyfriend and friends while treating everyone else like trash. Then slammed the door and left.

Her words are starting to lose value to me, but there's still this inkling where I feel responsible and remorseful, like I genuinely am the monster she claims I am. It's really hard.
I can't just leave. I tried once with my boyfriend's help, but my mother held me back and took my devices to cut off contact. She says legal issues stop me — and there's some truth to it: my residence permit is tied to hers, so I can't leave independently until I get my C-permit in January. I need a job and a German exam to get there. Moving out just isn't simple.

Feedback appreciated, and sorry this is long.

*Edit; I wish to add because I feel like this is important to add. I earn an allowance for the work I do around the house. I earn 20chf per day. So that’s 400chf per month. She also pays for my health insurance, phone bill and travel card which is around 200chf. She has invested a lot in me financially. So this adds a bit more reason why I am doing all of this.

text:
AITA for fact checking everything?

I (40F) have gotten to the point in life where I check reputable sites and sources for pretty much everything I see on social media, or hear irl during conversations. There has been so much spread of misinformation over the past decade on social media that now I hesitate to believe anything I see or hear until I verify it.

And since I have been doing this for so long I generally have a more neutral opinion on a lot of divided issues, because more often than not I end up getting 2 sides to every story while verifying information. I usually end up I pointing out other perspectives, something I actively worked on in my 30s because I used to be one of those people who never bothered or cared to consider a different perspective than my own.

But I just end up being labeled as either contrarian or argumentative.

I keep getting told that I just *want* to disagree with people, or that I am purposefully trying to prove people wrong. Sometime people even say that I am disagreeing for the sake of disagreement. But a lot of times I genuinely am so flabbergasted by what I see or hear that it bothers me to think it could be real, so I check. It truly is just me needing to reassure myself that outlandish claims aren't real because **** man I am overwhelmed with how bad things have gotten in the world or how crazy people are, etc. So when people say "OMG did you see/hear ______" I say, "Oh that can't be real" and pull out my phone and show people how and why it's not.

It has gotten to the point where I even have to pull out my phone and fact check myself, because people make me feel crazy for saying something, and I question whether or not what I am saying is correct. Which feeds into their belief that I "just have to prove people wrong"

I find it extremely difficult to just agree with people just for the sake of it, or let them believe something that I don't think is true and check facts when they are not around, or just keep my opinion to myself instead of pointing out a different perspective. I feel like I'm stuck between their idea of arguing for the sake of arguing and what feels like me agreeing for the sake of agreeing.

I have now begun to alienate myself from coworkers and friends because I can't stop myself and it makes me feel like I'm the problem.

So AITA?
label: yta

text:
AITA for an automated message waking a potential client at 1:30 AM?
I run a very small independent business where I offer tarot and spiritual readings. I handle my own bookings, payments, scheduling, and client communication.
Yesterday, a potential client contacted me about booking a love reading. We discussed pricing, different reading options, and meeting in person. They wanted a face to face reading, and I offered to meet at a coffee shop. They said they were worried about becoming emotional in public, so they asked if I could come to their home instead.
I explained that all appointments require a 40% upfront fee because of travel and because I’m reserving that appointment specifically for them. They weren’t comfortable paying before meeting me and asked for a reference. I provided one from a previous client.
We continued talking and everything seemed fine. I sent them my Square payment link and explained that I only accept payments through my website/Square so everything stays properly recorded. They replied, “Okay thanks. Makes sense.”
Later that night, my booking system automatically sent them a text at approximately 1:30 AM saying, “Are you still interested?”
I did NOT send this message myself. I genuinely had no idea my booking system could send automated messages at that time.
The next morning, they messaged me saying:
“I can’t believe you texted me at 1:30 AM to see if I’m still interested in a reading?! Who does that?! You woke me up! That’s so unprofessional of you!”
I immediately apologized and explained that it was an automated message. I told them I would never intentionally contact a client at that hour and that I would be checking my settings to make sure it doesn’t happen again.
I completely understand why they were upset. If I had personally sent someone a message at 1:30 AM, I would also consider that inappropriate. However, I genuinely didn’t know the system would send it, and I apologized as soon as I became aware.
So, AITA for the automated message waking them up, even though I didn’t personally send it and had no idea my booking system would contact them at 1:30 AM?

I invited some of my local friends to join us at the game, and told them all to bring their student IDs so we could avoid the hefty student validation fee. Basically, how it works at my university is buying tickets without a student package requires a student ID to get through the entrance. Otherwise, you have to go through a different entrance and get split up from the group, and pay an expensive fee on top. 

The plan was to have each one of my friends from out of town exchange phones with one of my local friends, so my local friends could use the external ticket and their student ID, and my out of town friends could use the regular student tickets without needing student ID. This ensured nobody was split up and nobody had to pay a fee. For the most part, everybody is able to get through, and phones get returned to the people once we're past the gate.

text:
WIBTA if my boyfriend and I back out of a friend's wedding abroad?
Hi everyone,

Some background: six of us met through work: me (Laura), my boyfriend Tom, Jess, Mark, Ben and Anna. Ben is getting married in Mexico in four months and invited all of us. We all are 27-29 years old and live in England. We committed two months ago, pretty excited and without really doing the math or looking into the details. Our idea was a two-week vacation plus the wedding.

Since then, a few things have come up:

Time off: Jess and I work directly together, and my boss just decided we can't take vacation at the same time. Only one of us can go.

Costs: We expected flights around $900, with $1,200 as our max. Now they're about $1,400 per person, plus roughly three domestic flights if we travel around the country. All in, about $2,500 each.

Fear of flying: Tom is afraid of flying. When we committed, he assumed a direct flight and getting around by car or bus. Turns out both long-haul flights have layovers, plus the domestic ones. That's a real strain for him, and buses would take way too long.

Travel plans: Anna planned her own three-week trip with lots of hiking (which none of us want to do) and already booked everything. We could join her, but don't have to. We'd planned to share accommodation at the wedding, though, so if we cancel she'd need her own place.

Mark: If Jess stays home, Tom and I could go, but that would mean two weeks as a group of three with Mark, and honestly, we don't want that. We like him, but over time he's VERY exhausting. It wouldn't be a fun vacation. Mark could join Anna in theory, but he doesn't want to use that many vacation days or do the hikes.

Where we're at: Jess has good reasons to stay home: someone has to cover at work, her boyfriend can't come (so safety concerns too), and she doesn't have the vacation days for Anna's route. Tom and I are thinking about canceling too. Flying out just for the wedding week would still be $1,400 plus accommodation. To make up for it, we'd take the couple out to dinner afterwards.
We feel really guilty. $2,500 each is a lot, we're not that interested in Mexico as a destination, and we underestimated the flights given Tom's fear. But we hate being unreliable. We committed two months ago and the wedding is in four months. WIBTA if we cancel?

TL;DR: We committed to a friend's wedding in Mexico, but it's way more expensive than expected ($2,500 each), my boyfriend is afraid of flying and it'd be far more flights than we thought, and one friend can't get time off. I arrived first as the primary visa applicant. My first month was extremely difficult. I was alone, struggled with the language, worked remotely, and couldn't find an apartment due to a housing crisis. I ended up in a hostel for almost a month.

My mom told me her cousin's family lived in the same city and connected us. I had never met them, but they welcomed me and helped with almost everything: banking, insurance, government appointments, paperwork, and translation. They became my support system when I had no one.

When my partner arrived, our apartment wasn't ready, so we stayed with them for a week. We introduced him as my coworker and friend and paid rent.

My partner had lived abroad before and warned me to be careful around people from our home country because of conservative attitudes and potential judgment. He reminded me of our reasons for migrating and shouldn't automatically trust even family with our relationship. I agreed.

My partner was upset because I didn't consult him. He said it was too sudden and that we'd have to pretend again in our own home. We'd even need to arrange the second bedroom to make it look like we're sleeping separately.

I understand his point. Our home should be our safe space, and I shouldn't have invited people over without discussing it with him.

Both our families are far away, and these people were there for me when I was completely alone. They helped me settle into the country and are a big reason I got through that difficult period.
I also thought his birthday would give them a natural opportunity to get to know him better, with him being the focus of the gathering.

I apologized for not consulting him, but I feel like he's overreacting somewhat. He pointed out that we paid rent while staying with my relatives, which is true, but this isn't about money. I told him it matters because what happens at his company directly and massively affects the shared project, it does matter a whole deal. She still refused.
She then told me that she genuinely intended to sleep with someone that night because she was trying to cope with something she was going through. If anything, that made me feel even more strongly that she wasn’t in the best state to make that decision.
But the whole standoff went on for way too long. She was essentially having a drunken tantrum in public, and everyone was exhausted. Eventually, some of our other friends convinced me that we’d already done what we could and that we should let her make her own decision. So I backed off and let her go.
Since then, the group has basically gone back to pretending everything is normal with her, while things between us have been awkward. I’ve been avoiding her because I don’t really know how to act around her anymore.

She wants to become a French pastry chef and eventually moved to New York, but due to the cost of living, she moved back in with her parents.

While living with them, her parents gave her a dog, “Bud.” She apparently didn’t want a dog at first, but eventually became attached to him.

Around the same time, I was dealing with a roommate who broke our lease, leaving me scrambling to find somewhere to live. I had two cats, had just started a seasonal job, and wasn’t sure how long the job would last.

Kay offered to watch my younger cat for two months so I could stay with my parents, save money, and make sure I had stable employment. She also asked if I would move in with her because she was struggling to live with her parents. I agreed, and we’ve now lived together for about nine months.

The problem is Bud.

We don't have a backyard, so he has to be physically walked outside whenever he needs to relieve himself. Since moving in, I've noticed Kay often doesn't take him out consistently. This happens almost every day, and there have been many occasions where Bud has gone 12–20 hours without being taken outside.

I work from home and used to take him out during my breaks because I care about him and didn't want him to be uncomfortable. However, it’s becoming difficult. I only get two 15-minute breaks and a 30-minute lunch, and I have my own responsibilities and two cats.

Kay has to wake up around 2–2:30 AM for work, but she sometimes wakes up late and leaves without taking Bud out. She gets home around noon or 1 PM, but instead of taking him out, she'll often spend 30–40 minutes talking to her long-distance boyfriend while waiting for DoorDash. Then she'll eat and go to sleep. She usually doesn't take Bud out until after 5 PM.

When I've brought this up, she says she's too tired and needs time to unwind. She hasn't directly asked me to take Bud out, but I can tell she gets upset when I don't.

I've suggested that maybe her parents could take Bud back or that she find him a good home, because I don't think she has the time or energy to properly care for him. She refuses and says she loves him and won't give him away.

I don't think she's a bad person, and I believe she loves Bud. But loving a pet and having the time and ability to properly care for one are two different things.

I feel guilty because I know Bud needs to go outside, and I've helped in the past. But he is not my dog. I already care for my own pets, and I don't think I should have to rearrange my workday because Kay isn't taking care of hers.

So, AITA for no longer taking Bud out during my workday? Should I continue helping because I know he can't take care of himself?

text:
AITA for the way I treated a guy at the club?

So this happened three days ago and I feel like shit.

Two friends and I (all around 19, F) were at the club and had a great time dancing like there's no tomorrow.

One of them went out to smoke while I and the other friend were still dancing. After a while we went up to the rooftop in order to look for her. There we saw her talking with two guys and we went up to them. They were really nice, just a few years older, and we started introducing ourselves. They spoke the local dialect and were outgoing, which I found very likable. During all of this I already thought one of them was really cute and felt like he thought the same about me. We continued talking and it was really fun. So long story short: He bought me a drink, we flirted and eventually kissed in front of the bar, continued talking on the rooftop etc. Basically: We hit it off. The evening went on and it was great.

And now we get to the asshole part:

Later that night me and my friends wanted to leave, so I told my friend that I wanted to say goodbye. I went up to him, told him that it was a nice evening and asked if he wanted my number, but he didn't understand me over the music. Instead, he said something along the lines of "If I go with you, I can't get back to the place where I'm from with the train" in a flirty tone. And in the moment I thought that might be insinuating hooking up with me.

But retroactively I'm not actually sure... He could have just meant going with us and talking would make him miss the train, Idk. I honestly wouldn't have minded either way.

But as I repeated what I said and he still couldn't understand me and neither could I really understand him, I was starting to get frustrated. I was tired and started to think about whether I'm making the right decisions. I also thought that his home is too far away from the place I'm going to move to. (And I was so wrong about that; completely misjudged the distance: It's actually just a 30-minute drive away!) And then I, like an absolute moron, just told him: "Today I'm not going anywhere with you", turned around and left. My friend told me after that he looked very awkward and unhappy :(

And I feel so sorry!! It must have felt like I was sending mixed signals and as if I was just playing with him the whole time, which was not the case at all! I was just sort of frustrated because we couldn't understand each other, tired, felt really overwhelmed with the situation and got cold feet in the last second. But I really didn't want to end it like that. I wish I had at least told him that I had a great time, that I think he's a wonderful person and that I wish him the best. But yeah, didn't do that and now I feel like shit.

So am I the asshole or am I just incompetent?

My family parks all our cars out in the driveway, and the car I drive is like 2009 old, so bad weather conditions concern me. But also sounds convenient when it snows to just remove the cover instead of spending 5-10 min in the early mornings wiping snow off the car.

For Christmas, my friend gifts me and my sister 2 car covers. It was a full body car cover size XXL. My sister didnt want it, obviously, since the windshield covers were smth only I've ever wanted. But 2 car covers weren't quite what I had in mind either.

My family has all sizes of cars from mini van, to SUV, to a sedan which I drive. The covers aren't OSFA. It also seems like a hassle or about the same amount of time to wrap my car up and then also have to remove it and store it away. Esp when all cars are used pretty much daily. When the cover is removed from its vacuum sealed package, it's pretty large and hard to fold back up. Kind of inconvenient overall.

Another thing is that my family home is cluttered, and he knows that. I have no need for 2 covers since my sister doesn't want it, and I'm really trying to not keep stuff we won't use in order to declutter the house.

Ive gotten gifts with a receipt for if I wasn't satisfied with the gift before. And once, for another friend, a part of a gift I got them was a duplicate with smth they already had, and I offered to return the copy which they accepted and gave it back.

Because he got 2, I looked up the product and found it on Amazon. I assume he spent at least $60-$100 on these gifts. After debating with myself, I ended up thanking him but admitted the following message:

"idk how to ask. would you be sad/offended if I wanted to return at least one LOL if you're still able to that is idk when you bought em"

He said depends on the reason, so i listed he could get his money back, the other family members likely won't use it so idk what to do with it, and I didnt get him a gift this year.

He responded only one was mine, so I said I appreciated how attentive he was to catch what I wanted in convo but dont want his money to go to waste in which he joked but truthfully said "Lol how I spend my money is my business " so i just said he's right and thanked him again. Also clarified later my sister had nothing to do with this (didnt want him thinking she asked to return it) and he also clarified he wasnt mad.

I felt bad tho and imo asking him to return the gift was an AH move, but I really didn't want to keep them either. Luckily, we're still friends haha but dunno how he felt about me asking.
